description: config.v2 §2.3, §2.5 to §2.14, §2.17: sequences of calls, device results and clock instants on one owner of the test contract `contracts/rfcfg.v1.toml` -> what it puts, replies and publishes, on config.v2's wire. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked, never blessed. config.v1's lifecycle.json holds every rule this file does not restate; these cases hold what config.v2 adds: the record put before the reply, the reply's as-of mark, tokens, times and the forms. setup: service; epoch, E in seconds; runs, the runs the owner takes in order, each {width, run}: its first at the start, the next whenever it takes a new run (the seq or the token counter spent, or a restart); counters, the token counter each run starts at, in the same order; seq_start, the first run's first seq where it is not 0; startup ({group: {parameter: {value, source}}}: the startup file's or the default values), overlay (the persisted layer, {group: {parameter: value}}), floor_s, apply_after_ms (the device states apply_at as the instant the set was received plus this), persist (whether the owner has a persisted layer), writable (the allowlist). `start` is the start: the owner puts its record before its tokens. Each step has t, milliseconds since the Unix epoch on the owner's clock, and do: set (group, fields, the Set<T> request's JSON reading, and hex, the query's payload; call, the O7 metadata {actor, request_id}, or absent), confirm, cancel, extend or persist (fields, a Control's, and hex), due (every act owed at t: the undo when the deadline has come, else each reach apply whose apply_at has come, earliest first), or restart (a new instance, taking the next run; the persisted layer survives it). device lists the device's results for the acts the step makes, in order: "ok", {"refused": words} for an apply, or {"failed": words, "readback": {group: {parameter: value}}} for an undo; a missing result is "ok". expect.acts lists the device acts, apply or undo. expect.puts lists the record's puts, in order, each {run, seq, record (config.v2's reading, as records.json writes a state), hex (the put's payload: CH form 0, the stamp, the record)}. expect.reply is null for due and restart, else {value: {run, seq, record, hex}} (form 2) or {error: {run, seq, code, cause, app, message, hex}} (form 3, Error's tag, the detail an Error record when app is set). The run and seq are the as-of mark: the run the owner writes under, and the last seq it minted under it, 0 for none. A replayed first answer (§2.14) is the first answer's bytes, its mark included. A message is sent with device_refused alone, the device's words, and never for a change that carries a sensitive value. expect.events lists the change events, each {run, seq, event}: config.v2.json's ConfigChangeEvent, its edits in the contract's order of groups, then of parameters. The owner mints no seq between a put and its reply, and publishes a change's event after its reply, or after its put when no call is answered.

cases.note: a hot set without a window: the owner applies, puts the record, replies with it under the put's seq, then publishes the event (§2.3, §2.6, §2.9, §2.17)

a reach set: the record pending, then the reply before the apply; a confirm before it is busy, in the error form under the mark; the apply puts again; the confirm answers the record, and its event follows; a second confirm is not_found

times rounded up and acted on at the instant stated: received 300 ms into a second, the floor's 10 s ends at 11 s, not 10.3 s; apply_at 1.3 s becomes 2 s; nothing is owed at 10.999 s; at 11 s a confirm is busy, the undo then runs, and a confirm after it is not_found (§2.8, §2.11)
extend and cancel answer the record: the extend's deadline rounded up from its receipt; the cancel undoes at once and its event follows its reply (§2.10)

the device refuses: app, its Error detail device_refused, the device's words as the message; nothing put, no token minted, the mark the last put's. A refused change carrying a sensitive value sends no message (§2.5, §2.9, §2.15)
a dry run answers the record as it would read, would_be set; it puts nothing and mints nothing, so the next change takes the run's first token (§2.9)

persist: the values the last change set become startup values, their sources overlay, and the record is put; a second persist changes nothing, puts nothing, and answers the record under the same mark; a restart starts from the overlay (§2.13)

an idempotent retry is answered the first answer, byte for byte, its as-of mark included, though the owner has put since; the key under another request is invalid_request, not kept; at 300 s the key is forgotten (§2.14)
a refusal is a first answer too, replayed byte for byte; a restart forgets every key, so the same request is answered anew, under the new instance's mark (§2.14)

the token counter's end: the run's counter starts at 65534, so its second token is its last; before a third, the owner takes a new run, whose counter starts afresh, and the record's instance stays the first run (§2.6)
the seq's end: the put takes the run's last seq, and the event after it a new run's first; the instance stays the first run, and the next token is the new run's (core §4.3, §2.3, §2.6)

a restart during a pending change: a new instance, its first run a 32-bit run drawn at random, revision 0, nothing pending; a late confirm is not_found, and the record's instance shows the restart (§2.12)

a join: the record's groups are bits in the contract's order; apply_at is the last joined reach group's while it waits; a hot join applies at once; the event's edits follow the contract's order, not the join's (§2.3, §2.7, §2.17)
a reach join that could not apply before the deadline is busy; once extended, it joins (§2.5 row 13, §2.10)
an empty change: an act that sets no value, the revision moved, the record put and an event with no edits, as any other change's (config.v1 §2.5)
an undo that fails ends partial: a value not read back is unknown, its source and value left out of the record (config.v1 §2.11)
a request that does not parse is invalid_request, under the mark; an owner with no persisted layer refuses persist unavailable, cause config
